title: Whose guesses of one minute were closer?
description: Two groups guessed when a minute had passed; their dot plots are compared by mean, median, spread and how many were near sixty seconds. Keeko doubts that the first group did better because its median is exactly sixty.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare groups by centre and spread together. The book prints 59.28 for the second group's mean; the data gives 1660 ÷ 28 ≈ 59.29. The counts 33, 28, 20 and 19 are read from the figure. Watch for children who decide by one measure alone.

source: The first group's 33 estimates run from 42 to 68 seconds, wi
video_script.why: The child can read a dot plot and the mean and median and now judges which group did better.
video_script.substitution: Closeness to sixty is judged by the centre and by how tightly the dots gather around it.
video_script.anchor: First group, 33 estimates: 42 to 68 seconds, mean ≈ 58.21, median 60. Second group, 28 estimates: 47 to 71 seconds, mean ≈ 59.29, median 59.5.
video_script.wrong_move: crowns the first group because its median is exactly sixty, although a few very early guesses pull its mean down and its dots spread wider
video_script.payoff_line: The second group did slightly better

final_answer.value: the second group, mean 59.29 closer to 60 and a smaller range of 24 seconds
final_answer.spoken: the second group did slightly better

maths_rules: first group: 33 values, 42 to 68, spread 26, mean 1921 ÷ 33 ≈ 58.21, median 60, 20 of 33 within 55 to 65
second group: 28 values, 47 to 71, spread 24, mean 1660 ÷ 28 ≈ 59.29 (the book prints 59.28), median 59.5, 19 of 28 within 55 to 65
ten-second guesses, group one 8, 9, 10, 9 and group two 7, 10, 10, 10; means 9 and 9.25; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: centre and spread together. Two dot plots on a seconds line stay in the anchor; a band from 55 to 65 is shaded; a table builds on the stage.
open_questions: The counts 33, 28, 20 and 19 come from the figure, not the book text, so they are not independently verified.

<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which group guessed one minute more closely?

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>A perfect guess would be sixty seconds.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>We will compare the two groups by their means, their medians and how far their guesses spread.

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, find the mean of each group.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>The first group's guesses add up to one thousand nine hundred and twenty one.
<bookmark mark='s3'/>Divided by thirty three, the mean is about fifty eight point two one.
<bookmark mark='s4'/>The second group's guesses add up to one thousand six hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='s5'/>Divided by twenty eight, the mean is about fifty nine point two nine.
<bookmark mark='s6'/>The medians are sixty and fifty nine point five.

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, find how far each group spreads.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>The first group's guesses spread over sixty eight minus forty two, which is twenty six seconds.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>The second group's guesses spread over seventy one minus forty seven, which is twenty four seconds.

narration: <bookmark mark='e1'/>Step three, count the guesses within five seconds of sixty.
<bookmark mark='e2'/>Twenty of the first group's thirty three guesses fall between fifty five and sixty five.
<bookmark mark='e3'/>Nineteen of the second group's twenty eight guesses fall in the same band.
<bookmark mark='e4'/>That is a bigger share of the second group.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the second group did slightly better; mean 59.29 is closer to 60 and the spread of 24 seconds is smaller

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The second group did slightly better.
Both groups guessed well, but the second group guessed a little closer to sixty.
